Findings on the cause of death:

· An injury to the left temporal region consistent with blunt trauma. The wound edge is arc-shaped; consistent with a hard object with a rounded edge about 6 cm in diameter. A skull fracture beneath it.
· Carbon monoxide level in the blood 18%. Markedly lower than would be expected in someone who remained in dense smoke for a long time.
· Limited soot deposits in the airways. The findings suggest the person breathed for a short time in the early stage of the fire.
· The burns appear to have occurred after or at the time of death.

Assessment: the injury occurred before the fire. After being injured, the person may have survived unconscious for some time.

Detailed report of the fire investigator:

· There are no short-circuit or arcing marks on the electrical panel in the back room. The soot on the panel comes from smoke from outside.
· The direction of burning and depth of charring show the point of origin was the wooden shelving system in the archive/storage room.
· Flammable solvent residue at the foot of the shelves. Solvent in a restoration workshop is normal; however, the pattern of distribution is consistent not with a container tipping over but with being poured along the shelves. The solvent cabinet door was found open and two containers empty.
· At the foot of the shelves, residue of melted plastic and its internal circuit: consistent with a programmable timer socket. The metal frame of a small fan heater connected to the socket.
· In the office section, a metal desk lamp fallen to the floor beside the deceased. Its base is round, 6.2 cm in diameter. On the edge of the base, a trace of blood not fully destroyed by the heat.

Assessment: the fire did not start from an electrical fault but from a timed heat source igniting shelving material soaked in solvent.
FIRE INVESTIGATION REPORT

Preliminary scene assessment by the fire crew:

The fire started in the rear section of the workshop and spread to the office and work hall through smoke and heat. There is an electrical panel in the back room; there is heavy soot around the panel.

Preliminary assessment: possibility of a workplace fire of electrical origin.

No detailed investigation has been carried out. The fire investigation report is awaited for the exact point of origin and cause.
PRELIMINARY FIRE REPORT

Preliminary assessment by loss adjuster Oğuz Tezcan:

· 19 days before the fire (26 September) the business’s cover for movable works and equipment was increased by 240%. The change request and signature were given by Serdar Belen.
· Under the partnership agreement a change of cover requires the approval of both partners; there is no signature of Kerem Sarıgül in the file.
· The claim was notified on 15 October at 11.40 by Serdar Belen.
· The business owes a total of 3.1 million TL to two banks; the September instalments have not been paid.

Payment of the claim has been suspended until the investigation concludes.

The forensic examination showed the injury came before the fire and was consistent with a round object; the fire report showed the point of origin was the archive shelving, not the panel, and found the timer socket. The plate record and vehicle inspection tied Serdar’s car to Beyoğlu and to the plaster; the service corridor inspection tied the same plaster to the back street. The card statement and the insurance report revealed the fire had been planned before the fight.

The time of the incident is not the time of the crime: the camera saw 02.14; the crime was committed at 00.05. Melis’s motive, her lie and her presence at the scene did not make her the culprit. And do not confuse a result with its purpose: the fire covered up Kerem’s death, but it was not set up for it.
Beyoğlu, Tomtom — 14–15 October 2028

Belen & Sarıgül Restorasyon was heavily in debt. On 26 September Serdar Belen increased the insurance cover by 240% without Kerem’s signature, and on 10 October he bought a timer socket and a heater; his aim was to start a small fire while the workshop was empty. Kerem found out about the policy. On the evening of 14 October he first discussed Melis’s dismissal with her, then at 23.12 called Serdar and summoned him. Serdar left his phone at home and came over, pulled his car into the back street and went in through the service door. When Kerem said he would call the police, Serdar struck him with the metal desk lamp. Believing Kerem was dead, he set up the device he had prepared: solvent was poured on the shelves, the heater was plugged into the timer socket. At 00.15 he left by the service door; Erdal Kılıç saw him and kept quiet. The fire started at 02.11. Kerem was still alive at that point.
Who is responsible for Kerem’s injury, and how did it happen?
